title: Answer legal questions with checked sources and citations
summary: Researchers built L-MARS, a team of agents that searches the web and case law, then checks its evidence; they report more accurate legal answers than leading chatbots.
agent_role: Agents decompose the query, search, verify and synthesize an answer; no human in the loop during answering, with humans judging outputs in evaluation.
outcome: On LegalSearchQA (200 questions on 2025 law), authors report substantially better factual accuracy, less uncertainty and higher human and LLM judge preference
what_they_did: Researchers Ziqi Wang and Boqin Yuan built L-MARS, a team of agents for legal questions. One agent splits a question into smaller ones. Searches then run across the web, a local legal database and the CourtListener court-case archive. A checking agent asks whether the evidence is enough, from the right place and still current. A final agent writes the answer. They tested it on 200 new multiple-choice questions about 2025 law.
how_it_went: The authors report much better factual accuracy and less uncertainty than standard GPT, Claude and Gemini models. Both human reviewers and AI reviewers preferred its answers.
worth_knowing: It has two modes: a fast one-pass mode and a slower mode that keeps searching until the evidence is enough. The code is publicly available on GitHub.
prompt: Answer this legal question: [your question], for [jurisdiction]. First, break it into sub-questions and show them to me. Then search official and reputable sources, including statutes and case law, for each sub-question. Before answering, check that each source applies to [jurisdiction], is current as of [date], and actually supports the point. If evidence is missing, refine your search and try again. Give a final answer with a citation for every legal claim and note anything you could not confirm.

curation.rationale: Launch seed collection, researched from search results.
